summary: Hides or moves a brush or level entity for all players in a dimension, or switches one of the level's story layers. A brush is found by its mesh and the level's position for it, within 5 cm, an entity by its EntityGuid and a layer by its name. Edits are held in memory only, so a server restart ends them. Applying to the same object again changes the existing edit.

apply.summary: Applies an edit and returns it.

params.definition: `kind`, 'brush' by default, 'entity' or 'layer'; `name`, a brush's mesh path, objects/...cgf, or a layer's full name as World Architect's story_layers lists it (on the Kingdom Come: Deliverance map, kcd1_rataje, as that game's level names it, its GUID in braces); `guid`, an entity's 16 hex digits, dashes allowed; `at`, where the level placed it; `hidden`; `model`, a props catalogue mesh to stand in its place, as for LevelEdit.model; `material`, a game material to draw it with, as for LevelEdit.material; `hideParts`, parts of a brush's model not drawn, as for LevelEdit.hideParts; and to move it, `position`, `rotation` (a Quaternion, [x, y, z, w] or Euler degrees { x, y, z }) and `scale` (a number or Vector3, 0.01 to 100).
params.dimension: Optional: limits it to this dimension. By default it applies in all.

apply.exampleLua: kcds.world.LevelEdit.apply({ name = "objects/manmade/structures/logistical/fences/fence_4rod_01.cgf", at = kcds.math.Vector3.new(512.4, 830.1, 31.2), hidden = true })
apply.exampleCs: LevelEdit.Apply(new { name = "objects/manmade/structures/logistical/fences/fence_4rod_01.cgf", at = new Vector3(512.4, 830.1, 31.2), hidden = true });

all.summary: All active edits, or those in one dimension.

params.dimension: Optional: limits it to this dimension.

getById.summary: The edit with this id, or null.

restoreAll.summary: Removes all edits, or those in one dimension, restoring the objects as the level had them.

params.dimension: Optional: limits it to this dimension.

state.summary: A snapshot of the edit, or null once restored.

kind.summary: 'brush', 'entity' or 'layer'. A layer edit switches one of the level's story layers, the state a place is in (a yard before or after a siege, a forge broken or rebuilt): `hidden` turns it off, otherwise it is on. It needs no `at`, moves nothing and takes no `model`; restoring it gives the layer back as the level has it. On the Kingdom Come: Deliverance map the layers start as a new game of that game has them (farms not burnt, Talmberk's fort as it was, the Vranik camp in its first state, Pribyslavitz in ruins); a farm burnt is its layer state1 on and state0 off. There a layer edit switches all of the layer: its buildings and plants (with their collision) and its doors, chests, beds, lights and fires.
kind.exampleLua:
-- Nebakov's yard as it stood before the siege.
local before = kcds.world.LevelEdit.apply({ kind = "layer", name = "beforeSiege_cf5fd30a-16c1-49d6-be2e-eebaa2bec480" })
kcds.world.LevelEdit.apply({ kind = "layer", name = "afterSiege_cc65bb6c-512f-48a7-acaa-9faa773dfc40", hidden = true })
print(before.kind)

name.summary: A brush's mesh path, an entity's name or a layer's name.

guid.summary: An entity's GUID, or '' for a brush.

hidden.summary: Whether the object is hidden, or for a layer edit whether the layer is off. You can assign to it.

model.summary: The mesh standing in the object's place, or ''. Assigning a props catalogue mesh, by path or file name, replaces the object for all players with a static Prop owned by the editing resource, at the object's position or the moved one, with the definition's rotation. Assigning '' brings the object back, and restoring the edit removes the replacement. Throws a TypeError for a mesh not in the catalogue. A brush whose collision the game keeps in static physics without a node keeps that collision while out, which applies for now to most of a village's houses and props.
model.exampleLua:
-- A felled tree leaves its stump.
local treeEdit = kcds.world.LevelEdit.apply({ name = "objects/natural/trees/beech_a.cgf", at = { 1661.9, 2168, 35 } })
treeEdit.model = "stump_fagus_sylvatica_a"

material.summary: The game material the object is drawn with instead of its own, or ''. Assigning a material path as the game's objects name theirs, such as 'objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_empty' (backslashes, capitals and a .mtl ending are accepted), draws it so for all players; '' gives it its own back. A material the game does not have leaves its own. A layer edit has no material, and a plant keeps its own. Throws a TypeError for anything that is not a material path.
material.example:
const tubEdit = kcds.world.LevelEdit.apply({ name: 'objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_wide.cgf', at: [2980.195, 678.693, 50.835] });
tubEdit.material = 'objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_empty';
material.exampleLua:
local tubEdit = kcds.world.LevelEdit.apply({ name = "objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_wide.cgf", at = { 2980.195, 678.693, 50.835 } })
tubEdit.material = "objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_empty"
material.exampleCs:
var tubEdit = LevelEdit.Apply(new { name = "objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_wide.cgf", at = new[] { 2980.195, 678.693, 50.835 } });
tubEdit.Material = "objects/manmade/common_furniture/tubs/water_tub_empty";

hideParts.summary: The parts of a brush's model not drawn, by the names of its sub-materials (lower case): [] for none. Assigning a list of up to 8 names hides those parts for all players, the rest of the model and its collision unchanged; [] shows them again. Only this object changes, not the model's other copies in the level. The names come from the material the level gives the object, so the same mesh can name its parts differently: the Kuttenberg bathhouse's wide tub has 'proxy', 'water_tub', 'liquid' and 'proxy_water', another wide tub 'waterfall_layer2' for its water. When a list is applied, the game client's log names the object's parts ("LEVEL edit parts: ... its parts: ..."). Throws a TypeError for an edit that is not a brush's, or a list that is not one of part names.

moved.summary: Whether the object has been moved.

move.summary: Moves the object, and can also turn and resize it.

exists.summary: False once the edit has been restored.
exists.exampleLua:
if not edit.exists then
  print("restored")
end

clearMove.summary: Returns the object to where the level placed it.

restore.summary: Ends the edit, so all players get the level's object back.
